description: PMO resource-prioritization screen at /utilization-priority — ranks every current employee by how urgently they should be (re)utilized. Combines a system-computed priority (UP (System): P1·Red / P2·Amber / P3·Green, driven by a 0–100 Value Score) with a manager-set UP (Manual) dropdown. Eight columns: Employee Name (with designation + experience), Department, UP (System), UP (Manual), Availability, Value Score, Skills / Tech, Allocation. Sourced from FRD 'Utilization Priority' v0.4 plus the missing-input rule clarified 2026-09-04 (a null rating and a null designation each contribute 0).
businessRules: UP (System) Value Score = 0.50 × Availability + 0.30 × NormalisedRating + 0.20 × Seniority. Verified live against 785 distinct employees on 2026-09-04: 781 fit a real 1–10 rating exactly, and the 4 exceptions are people with no rating and no designation, whose score is the availability term alone — consistent with the same formula once both null inputs count as 0.

Rating is on a 1–10 scale (not the 1–5 the FRD assumes), sourced from Employee ▸ Advanced filter ▸ Overall Rating (slider aria-valuemin=1, aria-valuemax=10, step 0.1). NormalisedRating = rating × 10, so the rating term collapses to 3 × rating.

Seniority is designation-banded: no designation (N/A) → 0, any base designation (SE, DE, DOE, MLE, QAE, SA, CSA, AISE, IoTE, UIXD) → 33, any 'Sr. X' plus PM/CSM/DOL → 67, LE → 100. This generalises FRD BR-9, which scopes seniority to only three designations.

Tier thresholds are exactly as FRD §5.3 specifies and hold with zero violations across the whole population: score ≥ 70 → P1·Red, 40 ≤ score < 70 → P2·Amber, score < 40 → P3·Green. The P1 cohort floor is exactly 70.00 and the P2 floor is exactly 40.00, so both cut-offs are inclusive.

The under-utilized flag is raised at exactly Availability ≥ 30%, matching FRD §5.4 / OI-3. The tile's own tooltip states the threshold verbatim: 'Counts everyone with 30% or more of their capacity unclaimed. Measured on availability alone, not on the P1/P2/P3 tier.'
The three tier counts must always partition the population: P1 + P2 + P3 == total result count.
Setting UP (Manual) must never alter UP (System), the Value Score or Availability (FR-13 / BR-14) — confirmed holding in the live build.
Only TM, EM and PMO roles (plus Admin) may open the screen or edit UP (Manual). Employee, PM and CSM sessions are redirected to /unauthorized and are not shown the sidebar entry at all.

Effective Availability is a fixed pre-calculated field: switching the Employee module's timesheet-duration selector (Last 5/15/30 days, Last 3/6 months, All time) changes Log Hours but must leave Utilization Priority's Availability and Value Score untouched (FR-4 / BR-5) — confirmed holding.

Filter state is session-sticky: it survives navigating away to another module and back, and is mirrored into the URL (upSystemTiers, upManualTiers, onlyUnderUtilized, sortBy/sortOrder, search). Stored state wins over a deep link on load, so a deep link into an already-filtered session is ignored.

A null rating and a null designation each contribute 0 to the Value Score — neither is substituted with a neutral midpoint (clarified by the product owner 2026-09-04). So a person with neither scores exactly 0.50 x Availability. Confirmed live: 193 of 3,654 employees have no rating at all (excluded from both the 1.1-10 and the 1.0-1.1 Overall Rating bands in the Employee module), and in a 785-person sample every one of them also had no designation.

The list opening on the P3 cohort ordered by ascending Value Score is INTENDED behaviour, and the Value Score column is intentionally not sortable — both were reviewed and accepted by the product owner on 2026-09-04, overriding FR-14 / BR-12 / section 12.B. Do not re-raise either as a defect.
edgeCases: An employee with neither a rating nor a designation scores 0.50 x Availability and nothing else, because both absent inputs count as 0. Four such people were found live (Dimple Dodia, Bhavin Goyal, Parth Roy, Arnav Limbachiya) — the Employee module renders their designation as an em dash and excludes them from every Overall Rating band. The calculation is correct as shipped; what is still missing is the information icon on the row saying the rating is absent.

The list opens ordered by Value Score ASCENDING, so the P3 cohort fills page 1 — reviewed and accepted as intended on 2026-09-04. Page 1 of any filtered cohort is therefore that cohort's floor, which is how the tier-boundary tests reach the exact 70.00 and 40.00 edges without a Value Score sort control.
The Value Score column has an information icon and a filter but no sort control — accepted as intended. Order the composite score indirectly through the UP (System) tier filter instead.
Per-column sort and filter icon buttons render at opacity 0 until their column header is hovered — automation must hover the header before clicking, or the click fails actionability.

Filter popovers are Radix poppers portaled to <body> with role="dialog" and data-state="open"; they are NOT descendants of the column header. Selections only apply after the popover's own Save button.

Designation and experience are packed into the Employee Name cell ("<Name> <Designation> <Experience>", with an optional leading NP notice-period badge) rather than shown as the separate Designation / Experience Years columns §12.F specifies.
Emptying the grid (a search matching nobody) correctly drives every KPI tile to 0 rather than leaving stale counts, and shows 'No one to rank yet' / 'No employees match the current filters'.
Pagination is fixed at 100 rows per page with no page-size selector; §12.E.4 specifies a default of 50 with a 25/50/100 Show dropdown.
Clicking an employee row or their name does nothing — the §12.E.2 detail side drawer, the name-link-opens-profile behaviour and the department-click-adds-a-filter-chip behaviour are all absent.

UP (Manual) persists across reloads and confirms with a 'Manual priority updated.' toast, but records no attribution — FR-17 / OI-10 require who set it and when, and §12.E.1 requires a hover tooltip showing it.
The success toast auto-dismisses quickly; automation must start waiting for it before performing the write, or the confirmation can vanish before the assertion runs.
Saved filter presets (§12.D: 'High Priority Free', 'Under-Utilized Only', 'Completely Free', 'Not Manually Reviewed' plus up to 5 custom) do not exist in the build.

A missing rating is detected by inverting the score: (Value Score - 0.50 x Availability - 0.20 x Seniority) / 3 resolves to exactly 0. The inversion subtracts the row's own seniority, so this works whether or not the designation is also missing.
